metadata.title: feat(auth): add HTTP Basic Auth support for OAuth token exchange
metadata.author: bogdanmariusc10

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #4358
**Jira Issue:** https://jsw.ibm.com/browse/ICACF-28

---

## 📝 Summary
Adds HTTP Basic Authentication support for OAuth token exchange to enable compatibility with Notion MCP server and other OAuth providers that require RFC 6749 Section 2.3.1 compliant authentication.

**Problem:** Notion MCP server requires client credentials to be sent as an HTTP Basic Auth header (`Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`) during OAuth token exchange, but ContextForge was only sending credentials in the POST body.

**Solution:** Added configurable `token_endpoint_auth_method` parameter that supports both authentication methods:
- `client_secret_post` (default) - credentials in POST body
- `client_secret_basic` - credentials in Authorization header per RFC 6749 Section 2.3.1

**Changes:**
- Modified three OAuth flow methods in [`oauth_manager.py`](mcpgateway/services/oauth_manager.py): `_client_credentials_flow()`, `_exchange_code_for_tokens()`, and `refresh_token()`
- Added comprehensive unit tests covering Basic Auth flows
- Created Notion MCP server setup documentation

**Backward Compatibility:** Fully maintained - defaults to existing `client_secret_post` behavior when `token_endpoint_auth_method` is not specified.

---

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature / Enhancement

---

## 📓 Notes

**Configuration Example:**
```json
{
  "oauth_config": {
    "client_id": "your-notion-client-id",
    "client_secret": "your-notion-client-secret",
    "token_endpoint_auth_method": "client_secret_basic",
    "authorization_endpoint": "https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize",
    "token_endpoint": "https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token"
  }
}
```

**RFC Compliance:** Implementation follows RFC 6749 Section 2.3.1 for HTTP Basic Authentication, encoding `client_id:client_secret` as base64 in the Authorization header.

**Testing:** Added three new unit tests (`test_client_credentials_flow_with_basic_auth`, `test_exchange_code_for_token_with_basic_auth`, `test_refresh_token_with_basic_auth`) that verify:
- Basic Auth header is correctly formatted
- Credentials are NOT included in POST body when using Basic Auth
- Default behavior (POST body) remains unchanged

**Documentation:** Created comprehensive setup guide at [`docs/docs/using/servers/external/notion-mcp-setup.md`](docs/docs/using/servers/external/notion-mcp-setup.md) covering both internal and public OAuth connection types.

comments.body:
Please refactor this out to its own function.
This code is repeated verbatim here, line 1460 and line 1580 and if there are issues with it at any point there is no clear way to see that it would need to be fixed multiple times.

reviews.author: madhav165
reviews.body:
Minor RFC compliance gap in the Basic Auth header construction (lines 405, 1309, 1405).

RFC 6749 Section 2.3.1 requires the client_id and client_secret to be URL percent-encoded (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` per Appendix B) before combining and base64-encoding them. The current code skips that step:

```python
credentials_str = f"{client_id}:{client_secret}"
```

Should be:

```python
from urllib.parse import quote
credentials_str = f"{quote(client_id, safe='')}:{quote(client_secret, safe='')}"
```

This won't change behavior for Notion — their credentials are alphanumeric/UUIDs where `quote()` is a no-op. But it will break with any provider that issues credentials containing `:`, `%`, spaces, etc. Appendix B specifies the decoding obligation on the server side, so compliant servers expect the encoded form.

`urllib.parse` is already imported in this file (line 23).

A couple of other things I noticed:

- The older `exchange_code_for_token` (singular, line 534) wasn't updated, but it has zero production callers — all real traffic goes through `complete_authorization_code_flow` → `_exchange_code_for_tokens` (plural). So not a concern.

- In `_exchange_code_for_tokens` and `refresh_token`, when `use_basic_auth` is True but `client_secret` is falsy, the code silently falls through to POST body mode. The behavior is correct (public PKCE clients can't do Basic Auth anyway), but a `logger.warning` there would help catch misconfiguration.

reviews.author: madhav165
reviews.body: PR looks good now - all the feedback has been addressed cleanly.

commits.message:
feat: add HTTP Basic Auth support for OAuth token exchange

Add support for RFC 6749 Section 2.3.1 HTTP Basic Authentication in OAuth
token exchange flows to enable compatibility with providers like Notion MCP
that require client credentials in Authorization header instead of POST body.

Changes:
- Add token_endpoint_auth_method configuration parameter
- Implement Basic Auth in client_credentials_flow()
- Implement Basic Auth in _exchange_code_for_tokens()
- Implement Basic Auth in refresh_token()
- Add comprehensive unit tests for Basic Auth flows
- Add Notion MCP server setup documentation

The implementation maintains backward compatibility by defaulting to
client_secret_post (credentials in POST body) when token_endpoint_auth_method
is not specified or set to any value other than 'client_secret_basic'.

Closes #4358

Signed-off-by: Bogdan-Marius-Catanus <bogdan-marius.catanus@ibm.com>
